title: Add -m/--max-time flag to `broadcast` subcommand
description:
Add `-m`/`--max-time` flag to the `broadcast` subcommand (alongside the existing `-t` timeout flag).

**Semantics:**
- `-t N` (timeout): "If no message arrives on input within N seconds, exit 124." Discarded once first message arrives.
- `-m N` (max-time): "Hard deadline — quit after N seconds no matter what, even if data is still flowing." Never discarded.

Implementation:
- Add `max_time: Option<u64>` to the `Commands::Broadcast` variant
- Compute `max_deadline = max_time.filter(|&s| s > 0).map(|s| Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(s))`
- In the main broadcast loop (reading from linger), check `max_deadline` each iteration
- When `max_deadline` is exceeded, stop the linger reader, clean up input FIFO, exit 0
- 0 means no max-time (block forever), same as omitting

CLI:
```rust
Commands::Broadcast {
    path: PathBuf,          // input FIFO
    outputs: Vec<PathBuf>,  // output FIFOs
    #[arg(short = 't', long = "timeout", value_name = "SECS")]
    timeout: Option<u64>,
    #[arg(short = 'm', long = "max-time", value_name = "SECS")]
    max_time: Option<u64>,
},
```

Depends on: synctell-13c (broadcast implementation), synctell-4f2 (read -m implementation, for consistency)

title: Add -m/--max-time flag to `read` subcommand
description:
Add an optional `-m`/`--max-time` flag to the `read` subcommand that acts as a hard deadline.

**Semantics (distinct from -t timeout):**
- `-t N` (timeout): "If nothing happens within N seconds, exit 124." Discarded once first message arrives.
- `-m N` (max-time): "Quit after N seconds no matter what — even if data is still flowing." Never discarded.

On `read` without linger: `-m N` means read for at most N seconds, then exit (whether or not a message arrived).
On `read` with linger (`-l`): `-m N` means stay alive reading until either (a) N seconds elapse, or (b) signal. Once N seconds pass, exit cleanly with whatever was read.

Implementation:
- In `cmd_input`, accept `max_time: Option<u64>` parameter
- Compute `max_deadline = max_time.map(|s| Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(s))`
- In the read loop, after each successful read (linger mode), check if `max_deadline` has been exceeded
- In `read_one_message`, also check `max_deadline` alongside the existing timeout deadline — if max_deadline exceeded, return a new `ReadResult::MaxTimeReached` variant
- 0 means no max-time (block forever), same as omitting the flag

CLI wiring:
```rust
Commands::Read {
    path: PathBuf,
    #[arg(short = 'l', long = "linger")]
    linger: bool,
    #[arg(short = 't', long = "timeout", value_name = "SECS")]
    timeout: Option<u64>,
    #[arg(short = 'm', long = "max-time", value_name = "SECS")]
    max_time: Option<u64>,
},
```

Unit tests:
- `read -m 2` with no writer: exits after ~2s (exit 0, no data)
- `read -l -m 2` with writer: receives messages for 2s, then exits cleanly
- `read -m 0` behaves same as no -m (blocks forever)

title: Add synctell_broadcast MCP tool
description:
Add a `synctell_broadcast` MCP tool that exposes the broadcast functionality via the MCP server.

This parallels how read_oneshot, read_start_linger, read_stop_linger, and write are exposed.

Tool schema:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct BroadcastRequest {
    /// Path for the input FIFO to create
    pub input_path: PathBuf,
    /// Paths to output FIFOs (must already exist)
    pub output_paths: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Seconds to wait for first message. 0 = block forever.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub timeout: u64,
}
```

The implementation should:
- Create the input FIFO
- Start linger reader on input
- In a background thread, fan out each message to all output paths
- Handle write failures gracefully (log and continue)
- Return a handle or status that can be queried

For the MCP integration, this might be a blocking call that runs until timeout or signal. Consider whether it needs a stop mechanism similar to read_stop_linger.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New MCP tool `synctell_broadcast` is registered and visible in tools/list
2. Tool accepts: input_path (string), output_paths (array of strings), timeout (integer, optional, 0 = block forever)
3. Tool creates input FIFO, reads messages, fans out to all output FIFOs
4. Tool returns status info when stopped
5. Integration test: call synctell_broadcast via MCP, write to input, verify outputs

title: Implement broadcast subcommand
description:
Implement a new `broadcast` subcommand that reads from one FIFO and writes to multiple FIFOs.

```
synctell broadcast [-t SECS] <input-fifo> <output-fifo> [output-fifo...]
```

Behavior:
- Creates the input FIFO (like read does) and starts a linger reader on it
- When a message arrives on the input FIFO, it is written to ALL output FIFOs
- Linger is implicitly always on for the input (no -l flag)
- `-t N`: timeout — if no message arrives within N seconds, exit 124. Once a message arrives, timeout is discarded (same semantics as read -l -t)
- Output FIFOs must already exist (writer-side semantics) — if an output FIFO doesn't exist, log a warning and skip it for that write
- If an output FIFO's reader disappears, log a warning but continue broadcasting to remaining outputs
- The input FIFO is created at start and removed on exit (same lifecycle as read)
- Each output write should be best-effort: if the write fails, log to stderr and continue

Implementation approach:
- Reuse the existing linger reader infrastructure (start_linger / LingerReader)
- Spawn background threads for each output FIFO writer
- Main loop: read message from input linger, fan out to all outputs
- On timeout/signal: stop linger, clean up input FIFO, exit
acceptance_criteria:
1. `synctell broadcast -t 10 input.fifo output1.fifo output2.fifo output3.fifo` reads from input.fifo, writes each message to output1.fifo, output2.fifo, output3.fifo
2. Linger is automatically active on the input FIFO (no -l flag needed or accepted)
3. `-t N` causes the broadcast to exit after N seconds of inactivity (no writer on input) — exit 124
4. `-t 0` or omitted means block forever
5. Output FIFOs must already exist (they are NOT created by broadcast) — error if missing
6. If an output FIFO's reader disappears, broadcast continues with remaining outputs (doesn't crash)
7. Broadcast reads from stdin if input is "-" (following Unix convention)
8. Unit tests: broadcast fans out to 3 outputs, broadcast with timeout exits 124, broadcast continues when one output disappears
9. All messages end with newline (same as read behavior)

title: Verify and test -t timeout flag on read subcommand
description:
Ensure the -t/--timeout flag works correctly on the read subcommand with both linger and non-linger modes.

After the subcommand refactor (synctell-87i), the read subcommand already receives the timeout value and passes it to cmd_input(). Verify and test that:

- Without -t: blocks forever waiting for a writer
- With -t N: waits at most N seconds for the first writer, exits 124 if none
- With -t N -l: waits N seconds for first writer; once first message received, stays alive indefinitely
- With -t 0: treated as no timeout (block forever)

The underlying cmd_input() and read_one_message() already implement this correctly — this task is about verifying the wiring through the new subcommand and adding targeted unit tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `synctell read -t 5 my-fifo` exits with code 124 after 5s if no writer connects
2. `synctell read -t 3 -l my-fifo` exits 124 after 3s if no first writer; once first message arrives, stays alive until SIGINT
3. `synctell read my-fifo` (no -t) blocks forever until writer connects
4. `synctell read -t 0 my-fifo` behaves same as no timeout (blocks forever)
5. Timeout only governs the wait for the FIRST writer — once a message is received in linger mode, timeout is discarded
6. Unit tests covering: read with timeout no writer → 124, read with timeout + linger no writer → 124, read with timeout + linger first writer arrives → stays alive
7. Exit code 124 on timeout, 0 on success, 1 on other errors
close_reason: Completed. Fixed -t 0 bug (was timing out immediately, now blocks forever). Added 3 CLI integration tests verifying: timeout with no writer exits 124, timeout+linger no writer exits 124, -t 0 blocks until writer arrives. All 22 tests pass.

title: Refactor CLI: convert -i/-o flags to read/write subcommands
description:
Convert the current `-i` (input) and `-o` (output) CLI flags into proper subcommands `read` and `write`.

Current state: `synctell -i my-fifo` and `synctell -o my-fifo "msg"`
Target state: `synctell read my-fifo` and `synctell write my-fifo "msg"`

The `read` subcommand should:
- Take a positional FIFO path
- Support `-l`/`--linger` flag (keep reading after first message)
- Support `-t`/`--timeout` flag (seconds to wait for first writer)
- Support positional `message` argument (for backward compat via MCP)

The `write` subcommand should:
- Take a positional FIFO path
- Support `-t`/`--timeout` flag (seconds to poll for FIFO existence)
- Support positional `message` argument (if omitted, read from stdin)

The `mcp` subcommand stays as-is.

The global `-i`, `-o` flags and their `conflicts_with` logic should be REMOVED.

Preserve ALL existing behavior — the underlying cmd_input and cmd_output functions are correct, just rewire the CLI parsing layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `synctell read my-fifo` creates FIFO, reads one message, exits (same as old -i)
2. `synctell read -l my-fifo` keeps reading (same as old -l -i)
3. `synctell read -t 5 my-fifo` times out after 5s (same as old -t -i)
4. `synctell write my-fifo "msg"` writes message (same as old -o)
5. `synctell write -t 5 my-fifo` polls for 5s (same as old -t -o)
6. `echo msg | synctell write my-fifo` reads from stdin (same as old -o)
7. `synctell mcp` still works unchanged
8. Old -i/-o flags are gone — using them should error
9. All existing unit tests in mcp.rs still pass
10. All existing integration tests in mcp_integration.rs still pass (they use `synctell mcp`)

title: Implement synctell_read_stop_linger MCP tool
description: Implement the synctell_read_stop_linger MCP tool. Parameters: handle (string, required). Signals the background linger reader to stop via its AtomicBool flag, joins the thread, removes the FIFO, returns any unread messages from the buffer, and removes the entry from the global state HashMap.
acceptance_criteria: Calling synctell_read_stop_linger with a valid handle signals the background reader to stop, removes the FIFO, and cleans up. Returns any buffered messages. Calling it with an invalid handle returns an error. Tests pass.

title: Implement synctell_read_start_linger MCP tool
description: Implement the synctell_read_start_linger MCP tool. Parameters: path (string, required). Creates a FIFO and spawns a background thread that loops reading messages. Each message is queued in a thread-safe buffer (Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>). Returns a handle that can be used with synctell_read_stop_linger and synctell_read_poll (future tool). State management: a global HashMap of active linger readers keyed by path.
acceptance_criteria: Calling synctell_read_start_linger with a path creates a FIFO and starts a background reader. Returns a handle/ID. The FIFO stays alive accepting writers. Calling it again with the same path returns an error. Tests pass.

title: Implement synctell_read_oneshot MCP tool
description: Implement the synctell_read_oneshot MCP tool. Parameters: path (string, required), timeout (integer, optional, seconds). Creates a FIFO, blocks until a writer connects, reads one message, removes the FIFO, returns the message content. This reuses existing cmd_input/read_one_message logic but returns the data as a tool result instead of writing to stdout.
acceptance_criteria: Calling synctell_read_oneshot with a path creates the FIFO, waits for a writer, reads one message, removes the FIFO, and returns the message. Timeout returns an error with code 124. Tests pass.

title: Implement synctell_write MCP tool
description: Implement the synctell_write MCP tool. Parameters: path (string, required), message (string, required), timeout (integer, optional, seconds). The tool writes the message to the FIFO at path. If the FIFO doesn't exist and no timeout, error. If timeout, poll for up to N seconds. This reuses the existing cmd_output logic but adapted for MCP (returns structured results instead of printing to stdout).
acceptance_criteria: Calling synctell_write with a path and message creates the FIFO if needed and writes the message. Returns success confirmation. Calling it for a nonexistent reader path (without -t) returns an error with code 1. Tests pass.
